newsitem.title: USA: Georgia fixes revenue distribution glitch, for now.
newsitem.headline: Georgia fixes revenue distribution glitch, for now.

text.p: Georgia Department of Revenue installed a new series of computer programs enabling it to accurately track and distribute sales tax revenues, at least temporarily, state auditor Claude Vickers said Thursday.
Vickers described the new programs as "a patch" that will prevent new revenue distribution errors until the department gets an upgraded computer system.
"It solves the problem for fiscal 1997, which started in July. It does not go back," Vickers said.

Vickers reported in June that Revenue Department had lost track of $1.5 billion of sales tax revenues and had guessed how much to pay local governments in a 14-month period ending in May. The problems resulted in under- and overpayments that have yet to be sorted out, and prompted Cobb County to sue to the department.
Former Revenue Commissioner Marcus Collins, who has since retired, blamed glitches in the department's ancient computer system.

"They have developed several new programs. Essentially what they will do is extract data from a couple of the databases and present it in a fashion that allows the Revenue Department to account for it, and us to audit it," Vickers said.

"It solves the problem on a temporary basis. This has given us an 18-month to two-year window. The problems they had with their computer system are still there. We are just going to have to upgrade those systems," Vickers said.
Vickers' earlier audit also criticized the department's computer security, staff training and oversight controls.
In a letter to Gov. Zell Miller this week, he said the new programs would allow the Revenue Department to operate "in a responsible manner" until new computers are installed.
